name: Ente Photos
tagline: End-to-end encrypted photo backup, hosted or self-hosted
description: A photo service in which everything is encrypted on your device before upload, so the server never sees your pictures. Most people use Ente's paid cloud; the same server software can be self-hosted.
backing: Ente Technologies, funded by storage subscriptions

maturity.rationale: The apps have been open and externally audited for years; the server was opened in 2024. The hosted service is well proven, while self-hosting is supported but less travelled.

selfHosting.summary: The server runs with Docker Compose alongside PostgreSQL and S3-compatible object storage. The quick-start is easy; configuring storage properly and pointing the mobile apps at your own endpoint takes more care.

requirements.notes: Light, because search and face recognition run on your devices rather than on the server.

managedHosting.label: Ente Cloud
managedHosting.note: 10 GB free; paid plans beyond that, with data replicated in three locations

strengths: End-to-end encrypted: the server, and whoever runs it, cannot see your photos
The hosted plan is a genuine drop-in for people who do not want to run a server
Face recognition and search run on your own devices, so privacy is not traded for features
The desktop app imports Google Takeout directly, keeping dates, locations and albums
weaknesses: On-device indexing is slower and uses phone battery at first
Self-hosting works, but the paid cloud is clearly the main path
The web app is plainer than Immich's or Google's
Encrypted storage means you cannot browse the files on the server's disk
